mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate environment reduces the cost of capital for firms, increasing equity valuations and producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 2.0%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.0%, it signals aggressive monetary tightening that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) decline relative to real sales (RSAFS), it indicates weakening consumer demand that triggers negative equity returns due to reduced revenue growth expectations.
failure_condition: The joint condition HOUST/RSAFS < 0.001 occurs, but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: During high employment growth regimes (PAYEMS growth > 0.5% monthly), robust corporate earnings expansion drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS growth exceeds 0.5% monthly.

mechanism_narrative: Strong industrial production growth signals robust economic activity, increasing corporate profitability and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO growth exceeds 0.3% monthly.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts fall below 1300.0 thousand units, it indicates a contracting housing market that reduces consumer confidence and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when HOUST is below 1300.0.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 3.0%), central bank rate hikes increase discount rates and reduce equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: When employment growth (PAYEMS) is high and unemployment rate (UNRATE) is low, it indicates a tight labor market that fuels wage growth and inflation, prompting central bank tightening and negative equity returns.
failure_condition: The joint condition PAYEMS growth > 0.5% and UNRATE < 3.5% occurs, but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such periods.
